note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: MACCO's cross-modal masked concept modeling plus MCA/MIR losses improve CLIP compositionality, supported by benchmarks and analyses

nodes.name: CLIP shows bag-of-words behavior
nodes.description: Contrastive VLMs like CLIP struggle with compositional understanding (object relations, attribute-object binding, word order), partly due to single global-vector optimization and not exploiting compositional information in image-text pairs.

nodes.name: Hard negatives have drawbacks
nodes.description: Hard-negative approaches are costly, noisy, bias models toward superficial patterns, and can induce oversensitivity, ranking semantically equivalent captions incorrectly.

nodes.name: MACCO masked cross-modal reconstruction
nodes.description: MACCO masks compositional concepts in one modality and reconstructs them using the full features of the other (masked text plus full image predicts concept words; masked image plus full text predicts patch pixels), without constructing hard negatives.

nodes.name: Global-to-local semantic injection
nodes.description: A parameter-free global-to-local injection averages each local token with the global CLS feature, compensating for the causal text encoder's lack of future context and CLIP's weak local patch supervision.

nodes.name: MCA loss
nodes.description: The Masked-augmented Cross-Modal Alignment loss adds masked texts or images as soft negatives in the cross-modal contrastive objective.

nodes.name: MIR loss
nodes.description: The Masked-augmented Intra-Modal Regularization loss contrasts masked features with their full counterparts within each modality to prevent masked-feature collapse and stabilize training.

nodes.name: Total objective
nodes.description: MACCO's total loss is L_MCA + l1*L_MIR + l2*L_MLM + l3*L_MIM, fine-tuned from CLIP ViT-B/32 on about 110k MSCOCO pairs, with predictors discarded at inference so the CLIP architecture is unchanged.

nodes.name: State of the art on compositional benchmarks
nodes.description: MACCO-CLIP achieves state-of-the-art results across ARO, SugarCrepe, VL-Checklist, VALSE and What's-up, gaining over CLIP 14.4% (ARO-Relation), 5.8% (ARO-Attribute), 21.9% (ARO-Order) and 8.3% average on SugarCrepe.

nodes.name: Beats CLIP-FT and CLIP-CAE
nodes.description: MACCO-CLIP beats CLIP-FT (+8.8% ARO-Relation, +26.9% ARO-Order) and CLIP-CAE (+4.1% SugarCrepe Relation, +4.8% VL-Checklist Relation), attributed to explicit modeling of entity-relation/attribute dependencies.

nodes.name: Complementary to hard negatives
nodes.description: Adding MACCO to NegCLIP and CE-CLIP yields further gains, e.g., +3.1% and +1.9% on VL-Checklist Relation.

nodes.name: General performance mostly preserved
nodes.description: MACCO-CLIP loses only 1.5% zero-shot and 0.4% linear-probe average accuracy versus CLIP on 11 classification datasets while raising compositional average from 61.2 to 67.7.

nodes.name: Better syntactic and linguistic encoding
nodes.description: In SentEval probing, CLIP-FT degrades on three tasks while MACCO-CLIP improves on all four, and it improves SICK-R over CLIP-FT and CLIP-CAE (+4.8% Pearson).

nodes.name: Concept-aware embeddings
nodes.description: MACCO-CLIP caption embeddings are significantly more similar to relation and attribute phrase embeddings than those of CLIP and CLIP-FT.

nodes.name: Robust to hard positives
nodes.description: On the Hard Positive benchmark MACCO-CLIP beats CLIP-FT on all subsets, with a 4.6% gain on the SWAP augmented accuracy.

nodes.name: Ablations support each component
nodes.description: Ablations show both text and image reconstruction losses help, each auxiliary loss helps alone, MCA and MIR combine best with masked modeling, and global-to-local injection improves results.

isolated_nodes.name: Attribute binding remains harder
isolated_nodes.description: Both MACCO-CLIP and CLIP-CAE gain less on attribute tasks than relation tasks, consistent with prior findings that attribute binding is harder.

isolated_nodes.name: Detector need not be strong
isolated_nodes.description: A highly proficient off-the-shelf visual grounding model is not required, and MACCO is resilient to noisy detection results.

isolated_nodes.name: Consistent across backbones
isolated_nodes.description: Improvements are consistent across ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14 and SigLIP backbones.

structural_reasoning: Problem and method design lead to the training objective, whose effects are verified through benchmarks, hard-negative combination, downstream, linguistic probes, robustness and ablations.
